label: Rewrite
output:
"The ones on the roofs—the leap over the Cutwater last spring—six feet of yawning void, and you were on the far side of it before your boots even hit the stone."

Nettle’s stride hitched, a microscopic tremor, the first ungraceful thing Cael had ever seen her do. "Luck," she said. "Good feet. My gran’s bead." She traced the river-worn charm at her throat, a reflex so deep she plainly didn't know she was doing it. "Why."

"No reason. Long day." Because you and I are the same, Cael did not say. Because whatever you feel when you cross a gap that isn't there, I feel when I press my palm to a lamp that's eavesdropping on something beneath the world, and neither of us is supposed to be able to, and one of us has learned to mask it while the other hasn't noticed she has anything to hide.

They walked. The token hummed against her hip. Somewhere behind them, a soft cold blue lamp caught the edge of it and guttered, once, and steadied, and told no one anything.

"Ash District tomorrow," Nettle said, at the door of the glimmerworks, and grinned, and was gone before Cael's key was in the lock—not vanished, nothing so grand, just around a corner faster than a person could go, into a gap in the evening that closed behind her like water.
